study.title: Effect of Acupuncture on Functional Connectivity of the Limbic Network in Patients with Knee Osteoarthritis: A Resting State Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging Study
study.study_design: Randomized controlled trial with neuroimaging; resting-state fMRI study comparing KOA patients and healthy subjects at baseline, and three intervention arms post-treatment
study.randomization: Computer-generated table of random numbers; light-tight, closed-letter method to hide randomization sequence; 1:1:1 ratio
study.blinding: Doctors, evaluators, and subjects were blinded to grouping status; single treatment room for blind evaluation; efficacy evaluated by third party; statisticians remained blinded to group allocation and treatment assignments
study.population: Patients with knee osteoarthritis (KOA) aged 45-75 years and healthy subjects aged 45-75 years
study.inclusion_criteria: KOA patients: 1) Age 45-75 years old; 2) Meet the diagnostic criteria of knee osteoarthritis, right-handed; 3) Kellgren-Lawrence knee osteoarthritis radiological diagnostic grading standard grade I-III; 4) Good compliance. To receive treatment voluntarily and obtain the informed consent of the patient himself or his family. Healthy subjects: 1) right-handed; 2) Age 45-75 years old; 3) Good physical condition, after the relevant hospital examination proved that the indicators are normal, no symptoms of KOA; 4) Signed informed consent without participating in other clinical projects.
study.exclusion_criteria: KOA patients: 1) Combined with other knee joint diseases, such as tuberculosis, tumor, rheumatism; 2) Combined with knee joint contusion or other trauma; 3) Serious cardiovascular disease, liver and kidney function damage, immune deficiency; 4) Have severe drug and alcohol dependence, mania or schizophrenia; 5) With obvious headache, dysmenorrhea and other chronic pain diseases, head trauma history; 6) History of hyaluronic acid or corticosteroid injection within 3 months; 7) Received acupuncture, massage and other treatments within 8 weeks; 8) MRI contraindications, such as claustrophobia. Healthy subjects: 1) Pregnant or lactating women; 2) People with symptoms of depression or anxiety, chronic pain disorders, or a history of head trauma; 3) Individuals with a chronic history of insomnia and indigestion; 4) Addiction problems, such as smoking, alcoholism; 5) MRI contraindications, such as claustrophobia.

conditions.tissue_level_reasoning: The description confirms skin puncture with a 20mm needle, but insertion depth is explicitly 'not_reported'. The needle is left in place without manual manipulation, but without knowing how far it was inserted (could be 1-2mm superficial or full depth into muscle), tissue level cannot be determined. The needle length of 20mm is consistent with either superficial or deep insertion depending on operator technique. | RESOLVED: needle inserted but depth unclear → assumed Level 1

Identical parameters to cond_baseline_koa_placebo. Skin puncture is confirmed with a 20mm needle, but insertion depth is explicitly 'not_reported'. Without knowing the actual insertion depth, it is impossible to distinguish between superficial (Level 2) and full penetration (Level 1). No manipulation after insertion does not help resolve depth ambiguity. | RESOLVED: needle inserted but depth unclear → assumed Level 1

extraction_notes.note: Expectancy, credibility, and treatment blinding success were not assessed or reported for any arm. No instrument such as the CEQ or VAS credibility scale was used. This is a potential limitation for interpreting the placebo comparison.

Deqi sensation was not formally quantified with a validated instrument (e.g., MASS, SAPS). Deqi is only described as the intended goal of manipulation in the verum acupuncture group; no subscale ratings, VAS ratings, or participant reports of specific sensations (numbness, soreness, heaviness, etc.) were provided.

No neuroimaging results were reported for the waiting group (post-treatment vs baseline). The paper describes three arms with two fMRI scans each, but only the acupuncture group and placebo acupuncture group post-treatment ICA results are presented in the tables and figures.

The placebo acupuncture sham procedure uses penetrating needles at non-acupoint locations 1 cm away from the lateral median line of lower limbs. The paper states this was done 'to minimize the effect of comfort acupuncture' and that no further manipulation was performed after skin puncture. The penetration depth is not reported. This design may produce some needle sensation despite being labeled 'placebo.'

Table 6 row for Parahippocampal gyrus (R) shows MNI coordinates 2, 5, 31 with Brodmann 38. Coordinates 2, 5, 31 are unusual for parahippocampal gyrus and may reflect an OCR or typographic error in the original paper. The same coordinate set (2, 5, 31) also appears in Table 5 for Median cingulate and paracingulate gyri with Brodmann 24. This inconsistency is preserved as reported.

The paper reports 73 participants screened (from flowchart figure caption: 'Recruitment and Screening (n=73)') but the text states '72 KOA patients were enrolled in the trial.' This minor inconsistency is preserved as reported.
No scan duration (number of volumes) for the resting-state BOLD-fMRI acquisition is reported. TR=2000ms and layer number=50 are reported, but total scan time is not stated.
The paper does not report the frequency of acupuncture sessions per week (e.g., how many sessions per course, how many days per week), only '4 courses totaling 20 sessions' over 4 weeks.

No between-group neuroimaging comparisons (e.g., acupuncture group change vs placebo acupuncture group change) are reported. All neuroimaging contrasts are within-group pre-post or cross-sectional KOA vs healthy controls.

The Brodmann area column in Table 6 for Lenticular nucleus, pallidum (R) and Caudate nucleus (R) is marked with dashes ('—'), indicating no Brodmann area was assigned. These are preserved as 'not_reported' in the extraction.

The correlation direction labels in Table 8 are ambiguous for some entries. For entries labeled 'positive' (e.g., Lenticular nucleus putamen R / WOMAC pain score, r=0.545), this suggests that greater FC increase is associated with greater WOMAC pain score improvement; however, the sign of the clinical scale difference (pre minus post) needs careful interpretation. The r values are preserved exactly as reported without re-interpretation.
Supplementary Materials 1-6 are referenced but not provided in the PDF. These may contain additional data relevant to funding or methodology.

No baseline ICA or neuroimaging results were reported for the comparison between healthy subjects and individual KOA subgroups (acupuncture, placebo, waiting). The baseline comparison pools all 45 KOA patients against 15 healthy subjects.
